newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian feed market remains tight.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian feed market remains tight.

text.p: The Australian feed grain market remained tight which tended to support prices this week, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Friday.
However, an easing in Queensland and northern New South Wales (NSW) sorghum was seen in response to a fall in U.S. prices, the AWB said in its weekly grain market report.
The old crop feed grain market saw little wheat or triticale appear, it said.
In Victoria and South Australia old crop prices were supported by strong demand and grain being held on farm.
New crop sellers appeared reluctant at current prices although crop conditions are good at this stage, the AWB said.
"This could be attributed to concerns over the El Nino impact and worsening ABARE crop forecasts," it said.

In a special Crop Report, ABARE (Australian Bureau of Resource and Agricultural Economics) this week put its forecast of the 1997/98 wheat crop at 16.25 million tonnes, down from the record crop of 23.6 million tonnes in 1996/97.
In Western Australia, the market was quiet for old crop while growers received good rainfall to support current plantings and ease drought concerns, the AWB said.
The wheat market saw no significant movement with prices remaining unchanged or firming between A$2 to A$4 a tonne depending on location, the AWB said.
Central and southeasten NSW had good rains through the weekend easing concerns about dryness in this area.
The market, however, is still focussed on the dry weather in the Victorian and South Australian Mallee region and central Eyre Peninsula.
Some of these areas may turn to barley although the planting window extends to the end of July, the AWB said.
Old crop prices were underpinned by the tender results providing a price ceiling for the trade around the low A$180s a tonne delivered to port at Port Kembla and Geelong.

The AWB said NSW had a busy week in shipping with significant shipments to Japan and Pakistan. Queensland, Victoria and South Austeralia had a quiet week. Western Australia shipped a fair tonnage to Indonesia and Japan.
